transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function using an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` receiver parameter, named public target, and the generated `mid <= old(slice)@.len()` / `final(slice)@ == slice_rotated_left(old(slice)@, mid as int)` contract.

Preserved the target flow: `assert!(mid <= self.len())` is represented by a local source-shaped macro that calls an executable precondition helper, then `k = self.len() - mid`, `p = self.as_mut_ptr()` is represented by the reviewed `as_mut_ptr` dependency boundary, and the unsafe rotation call is preserved in `rust_1_96_rotate_left_ptr_rotate` as `rotate::ptr_rotate(mid, p.add(mid), k)`.
Reused the reviewed `core::slice::as_mut_ptr` start-pointer/final-frame shape locally instead of re-proving the raw slice-to-element pointer cast.
Isolated only the unsupported raw pointer `p.add(mid)` plus `rotate::ptr_rotate(mid, p.add(mid), k)` call in a named private boundary; the public target is not external_body.

Added a named bridge from the source-backed ptr_rotate effect and preserved start pointer/length arithmetic to the generated `slice_rotated_left` postcondition without making the public target external.
